errors.description: The final characterization is false as stated: primes absent from every initial number may occur in d with arbitrary positive exponent, since every positive exponent divides 0, so no unique maximal d exists without restricting its prime support.
errors.quote: the unique maximal $d$ with $v_p(d) \mid v_p(a_i)$ for all $p$ and all $i$.

parsed.notes: The actual proof of both parts is complete and correct. Termination follows from the product/number-of-ones argument, and the prime-wise gcd-of-valuations invariant uniquely determines M. Only the optional final remark needs qualification.
